It would also add to Boeing’s long-term backlog and provide greater production visibility as Indian airlines invest heavily to accommodate rising passenger demand.

Akasa currently operates 43 737 Max aircraft and serves 29 domestic and seven international destinations. The airline, which began flying in 2022, remains a relatively small competitor to IndiGo and Air India.
Akasa carried about 5.5% of India’s domestic passengers last month, compared with roughly 65% for IndiGo and 27% for Air India Group.

The potential order comes as Akasa seeks 10.5 billion rupees, or about $109 million, in equity and debt financing. The airline also has explored government-backed financing after the Iran war disrupted airspace and pushed jet fuel costs higher.

India’s commercial aircraft fleet has expanded from about 100 planes in 2000 to nearly 900 today, with more than 1,500 additional aircraft on order. IndiGo has roughly 900 planes awaiting delivery through 2035, while Air India previously placed a 470-aircraft order split between Boeing and Airbus.
For Boeing, another large Akasa commitment would deepen its exposure to that expansion and reinforce the 737 Max as its principal competitor to Airbus’s A320neo family in India.
